title: Durability under crash
objection: Redis loses acknowledged writes when it crashes.

claims.claim: default (appendonly no, no save) → 0/20,000 acknowledged writes survived SIGKILL (0.00%)
claims.detail: expected: total loss — nothing is persisted at all

claims.claim: RDB snapshots only (save 60 1000) → 0/20,000 acknowledged writes survived SIGKILL (0.00%)
claims.detail: expected: loses everything since the last snapshot

claims.claim: AOF, appendfsync everysec → 20,000/20,000 acknowledged writes survived SIGKILL (100.00%)
claims.detail: expected: zero loss on process crash; ~2s exposure to machine loss

claims.claim: AOF, appendfsync always → 20,000/20,000 acknowledged writes survived SIGKILL (100.00%)
claims.detail: expected: zero loss on process crash AND on machine loss

claims.claim: everysec: a write is exposed to machine loss for p50 1033.937 ms / p99 1060.268 ms / max 1133.19 ms
claims.detail: WAITAOF blocks until the write is fsynced but does NOT trigger an fsync, so this latency is exactly the wait for the next scheduled one — i.e. the exposure window, measured rather than assumed. Note the bound is ~2 s, not the 1 s the docs state: aof.c postpones the write() by up to 2000 ms when an fsync is already in flight.

claims.claim: always: exposure collapses to p50 0.262 ms / p99 0.87 ms / max 2.975 ms
claims.detail: every write is fsynced before the reply, so there is effectively no window

claims.claim: everysec vs no persistence: costs 42.5% throughput (377,424 → 216,900 ops/s)
claims.detail: expected: AOF writes are buffered and flushed once per event-loop iteration, and the fsync runs on a background thread — so everysec should barely touch the write path. That is what makes it the sane default.

claims.claim: appendfsync always costs 54.6% (171,323 ops/s) — far less than folklore suggests, because Redis group-commits
claims.detail: the AOF is fsynced once per event-loop iteration for a whole batch of clients, not once per command

claims.claim: recovery: 500,000 records across 4,000 keys reloaded from AOF in 0.28 s
